headline.headline: THUNDER SILENCED: SPURS EVEN SERIES WITH DOMINANT GAME 4 ROUT
headline.deck: San Antonio holds Oklahoma City to 82 points as series heads to Game 5 tied 2-2
headline.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- The Oklahoma City Thunder, the Western Conference's top seed and the most prolific offensive team in the NBA this season, ran into a wall Sunday night at the AT&T Center. The San Antonio Spurs dismantled them 103-82, evening the second-round series at two games apiece and sending a clear message that this best-of-seven is far from decided.

The 21-point margin represented one of the worst offensive efforts the Thunder have produced in years, a stunning reversal for a team that finished the regular season 64-18. San Antonio's defense smothered Oklahoma City's transition game and forced the Thunder into a grinding half-court contest they were never comfortable in, holding them well below their season scoring average from wire to wire.

Game 5 now looms as the decisive hinge game of the series, with home-court advantage having shifted and momentum squarely in San Antonio's favor. The Spurs, who finished the regular season 62-20, have now proven they can dictate the terms of a playoff series against the conference's best team. Victor Wembanyama and his teammates return to action knowing a road victory Tuesday would put them one win from the conference finals.

secondary.headline: STONE RETURNS, KNIGHTS PUSH AVALANCHE TO BRINK WITH 3-0 SERIES LEAD
secondary.deck: Vegas captain scores in comeback from injury as Colorado faces historic deficit
secondary.body:
LAS VEGAS -- Mark Stone had missed five games with a lower-body injury, but the Vegas Golden Knights captain chose Sunday night to make his return count. Stone scored as Vegas defeated Colorado to take a commanding 3-0 lead in their second-round series, pushing the Avalanche to the brink of elimination in a matchup that appeared far more even on paper.

No team in NHL history has ever come back from a 3-0 series deficit in the playoffs, and Colorado -- which finished the regular season 55-16-11 -- now faces that impossible arithmetic in Game 4. The Golden Knights, who went 39-26-17 in the regular season and were considered underdogs entering this series, have outplayed the Avalanche in every meaningful situation. Stone's return only deepens their advantage heading into what could be a sweep Monday night.

secondary.headline: PIRATES QUIET BLUE JAYS, 4-1, BEHIND RODRIGUEZ ON THE MOUND
secondary.deck: Pittsburgh scores twice in the sixth to put Toronto away at Rogers Centre
secondary.body:
TORONTO -- Yohandy Rodriguez earned the win Sunday as the Pittsburgh Pirates defeated the Toronto Blue Jays 4-1 at Rogers Centre, putting the game away with a two-run sixth inning that broke open a tight pitchers' duel. The Pirates had led 2-0 through two innings, saw Toronto scratch one back in the fourth, then buried the Blue Jays for good with the sixth-inning surge.

The game was not without its edge. Rodriguez hit Mangum with a pitch, Mitch Keller hit Vladimir Guerrero Jr., and G. Soto hit Gimenez as the benches stayed sharp throughout the 2-hour, 50-minute contest before 41,000 at Rogers Centre. Toronto, now 25-28, has dropped another game in the AL East standings while Pittsburgh continues to press for relevance in the National League Central.

secondary.headline: BAZZANA HOMERS BUT GUARDIANS EDGE PHILLIES, 3-1, IN PHILADELPHIA
secondary.deck: Cleveland's Herrin earns win as Guardians take series game at Citizens Bank Park
secondary.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- Cleveland's Guardians grinded out a 3-1 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies on Sunday, with reliever Herrin earning the win before 37,808 fans at Citizens Bank Park. The Guardians scored the game's first run in the fifth inning, added another in the sixth, and held off a seventh-inning Phillies run before tacking on an insurance marker in the eighth.

The Phillies offense showed life in the extra-base department, with Rhys Hoskins and Kyle Schwarber each doubling, but Cleveland's pitching stifled Philadelphia when it mattered most. The lone home run of the afternoon belonged to Cleveland's Bazzana, his third of the season, which proved to be the decisive blow. Herrin and the Cleveland bullpen did the rest, holding Philadelphia's powerful lineup to a single run in the final three innings.

column.headline: THE THUNDER ARE RUNNING OUT OF EXCUSES -- AND TIME
column.body:
Oklahoma City built the best record in the Western Conference this season. They were supposed to be the team nobody wanted to face in May. But after Sunday night's 21-point shellacking at the hands of San Antonio, serious questions deserve serious answers: Can this Thunder roster perform when the margin for error shrinks to nothing? Scoring 82 points against a Spurs team playing in their own building is not a blip. It is a warning sign posted in neon.

The Thunder still have the talent to win this series -- nobody should count out a 64-win team with two home games potentially remaining. But momentum is a real currency in a short series, and San Antonio just cashed a very large check. Victor Wembanyama is playing like a man who understands the moment. Oklahoma City needs to find out whether their stars can say the same before Game 5 tips off and this series takes a turn they cannot reverse.

story.headline: JUDGE WALKS IT OFF AS YANKS BLANK RAYS IN NINTH
story.deck: Homer in final frame gives New York 2-0 win over AL East leaders
story.body:
NEW YORK — Aaron Judge delivered the only offense either team would need, parking a two-run shot in the bottom of the ninth inning Sunday to give the New York Yankees a 2-0 shutout of the Tampa Bay Rays before 41,396 fans at Yankee Stadium. Judge's 17th home run of the season broke a scoreless deadlock that had held for eight and a half frames, handing the first-place Rays their second loss in a row.

The game was a pitchers' duel through eight innings, with neither side managing a run. Tampa Bay, which came in at 34-16 atop the AL East, left 12 runners on base and could not push any of them across. New York's bullpen held the line until Judge ended the suspense in the ninth, with a baserunner who had entered to run for Trent Grisham also coming around to score. Yasiel Diaz contributed a double among the Yankees' limited output.

Elsewhere Sunday, the Minnesota Twins edged the Boston Red Sox 6-5 in a back-and-forth affair at Fenway Park, with Minnesota scoring three runs in the sixth inning to break a 3-3 tie and hold on despite a Boston run in the ninth. William Contreras hit his 11th homer of the year for the Twins, while Masataka Yoshida connected for his first of the season for the Red Sox in a losing cause. The Twins stranded 24 runners, but did just enough to escape Fenway with the win.

story.headline: WEMBANYAMA LEADS SPURS PAST THUNDER TO TAKE SERIES LEAD
story.deck: San Antonio dominates Game 4 to even Western Conference Finals at 2-2
story.body:
SAN ANTONIO — Victor Wembanyama set the tone early and never let up, powering the San Antonio Spurs to a commanding 103-82 victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday night at the AT&T Center, evening the Western Conference Finals at two games apiece. The Spurs, finishing second in the West at 62-20, handed the conference's top seed its worst offensive performance in years, leaving the Thunder stunned and searching for answers heading into a pivotal Game 5.

Oklahoma City, the Western Conference's top seed at 64-18, managed just 82 points on what observers described as a flat, lifeless offensive night. The Thunder, who entered the series as favorites, could not find rhythm against San Antonio's swarming defense. ESPN's Stephen A. Smith pulled no punches in the aftermath, declaring on SportsCenter that Oklahoma City was quote flat all night unquote, a sentiment that echoed across the basketball world as the 21-point margin told the story plainly.

With the series now deadlocked at 2-2, the stakes could not be higher as the two teams prepare to meet again in what promises to be a pivotal Game 5. Wembanyama's performance in Game 4 served as a reminder of his singular ability to alter a series with his combination of length, shot-blocking and offensive versatility. San Antonio now carries momentum into the next contest, while Oklahoma City must regroup and find the offensive aggression that carried the Thunder to the best record in the Western Conference during the regular season.

boxScores.title: San Antonio Spurs 103, Oklahoma City Thunder 82

story.headline: STONE RETURNS, KNIGHTS ROLL AS AVALANCHE FACE HISTORIC HOLE
story.deck: Vegas captain scores in comeback game as Colorado trails series 3-0
story.body:
LAS VEGAS — Mark Stone had missed five games with a lower-body injury, and the Colorado Avalanche had reason to hope his absence might last a little longer. It did not. The Vegas Golden Knights captain returned to the lineup Sunday night, scored, and helped push Vegas to a 3-0 series lead over the Avalanche, leaving the Stanley Cup favorites staring down one of the most daunting deficits in playoff hockey.

The situation grew darker still for Colorado when center Nathan MacKinnon was hobbled after blocking a shot in the second period. MacKinnon, the engine of an Avalanche squad that posted a 55-16-11 regular-season record in the Central Division, visibly labored after the blocked shot, raising immediate concerns about his availability for Game 4 on Tuesday. Vegas, which finished the regular season at 39-26-17 in the Pacific Division, has now outplayed a superior team on paper through three consecutive games.

No NHL team has ever overcome a 3-0 series deficit to win a playoff series, and Colorado will need MacKinnon healthy and Stone neutralized to have any hope of forcing a Game 5. Game 4 is scheduled for Tuesday in Las Vegas.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS TEAMS SCRAMBLE TO FIND THEIR FRANCHISE SIGNAL-CALLER
story.deck: Several clubs made bold moves this spring to address the game's most critical position.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has turned into a full-blown quarterback market frenzy, with front offices across the league making aggressive moves to secure their long-term answers under center. The Las Vegas Raiders, fresh off another disappointing campaign, agreed to terms with veteran quarterback Sam Darnold on a three-year contract worth $102 million, signaling a commitment to stability after cycling through starters for the better part of a decade. Meanwhile, the New Orleans Saints parted ways with longtime starter Derek Carr and immediately began pursuing trade options, with league sources indicating the Cleveland Browns entered preliminary discussions about a potential swap of draft assets.

The 2026 NFL Draft produced its share of instant analysis fodder, with Shedeur Sanders sliding unexpectedly to the third overall pick before landing with the Carolina Panthers, who surrendered a package of future selections to move up and secure the Colorado product. Draft analysts pointed to pre-draft interview concerns as a contributing factor in his fall, though Panthers general manager Dan Morgan expressed full confidence in the selection at the team's post-draft press conference. Defensive tackle Mason Graham out of Michigan went first overall to the Jacksonville Jaguars, who prioritized bolstering a defensive front that ranked among the worst in the league last season.

On the coaching front, the Chicago Bears made waves by hiring former Green Bay Packers offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich as their new head coach, tasking him with building a system around third-year quarterback Caleb Williams. Training camp storylines are already forming around Williams, who spent the spring working closely with his new staff in a voluntary minicamp that drew strong attendance from key veterans. The Bears, who finished 7-10 in the 2025 season, are banking on continuity and offensive development to finally push them back toward playoff contention in the NFC North.
